chapters.arabic_text:
### | الظاهر الباطن

هذان الوصفان أيضا من المضافات فإن الظاهر يكون ظاهرا لشيء وباطنا لشيء
ولا يكون من وجه واحد ظاهرا وباطنا بل يكون ظاهرا من وجه بالإضافة  إلى
إدراك وباطنا من وجه آخر فإن الظهور والبطون إنما يكون بالإضافة إلى
الإدراكات والله سبحانه وتعالى باطن إن طلب من إدراك الحواس وخزانة الخيال
ظاهر إن طلب من خزانة العقل بطريق الاستدلال فإن قلت أما كونه باطنا
بالإضافة إلى إدراك الحواس فظاهر وأما كونه ظاهرا للعقل فغامض إذ الظاهر ما
لا يتمارى فيه ولا يختلف الناس في إدراكه وهذا مما قد وقع فيه الريب الكثير
للخلق فكيف يكون ظاهرا فاعلم أنه إنما خفي مع ظهوره لشدة ظهوره فظهوره سبب
بطونه ونوره هو حجاب نوره وكل ما جاوز حده انعكس على ضده
ولعلك تتعجب من هذا الكلام وتستبعده ولا تفهمه إلا بمثال
فأقول لو نظرت إلى كلمة واحدة كتبها كاتب لاستدللت بها على كون الكاتب
عالما قادرا سميعا بصيرا واستفدت منه اليقين بوجود هذه
الصفات بل لو رأيت كلمة مكتوبة لحصل لك يقين قاطع بوجود كاتب لها عالم
قادر سميع بصير حي ولم يدل عليه إلا صورة كلمة واحدة وكما تشهد هذه الكلمة
شهادة قاطعة بصفات الكاتب فما من ذرة في السموات والأرض من فلك وكوكب وشمس
وقمر وحيوان ونبات وصفة وموصوف إلا وهي شاهدة على نفسها بالحاجة إلى مدبر
دبرها وقدرها وخصصها بخصوص صفاتها بل لا ينظر الإنسان إلى عضو من أعضاء
نفسه وجزء من أجزائه ظاهرا وباطنا بل إلى صفة من صفاته وحالة من حالاته
التي تجري عليه قهرا بغير اختياره إلا ويراها ناطقة بالشهادة لخالقها
وقاهرها ومدبرها وكذلك كل ما يدركه بجميع حواسه في ذاته وخارجا من ذاته
ولو كانت الأشياء مختلفة في الشهادة يشهد بعضها ولا يشهد بعضها لكان
اليقين حاصلا للجميع ولكن لما كثرت الشهادات حتى اتفقت خفيت وغمضت لشدة
الظهور ومثاله أن أظهر الأشياء ما يدرك بالحواس وأظهرها ما يدرك بحاسة
البصر وأظهر ما يدرك بحاسة البصر نور الشمس المشرق على الأجسام الذي به
يظهر كل شيء فما به يظهر كل شيء كيف لا يكون ظاهرا
وقد أشكل ذلك على خلق كثير حتى قالوا  الأشياء الملونة ليس فيها إلا
ألوانها فقط من سواد وحمرة فأما أن يكون فيها مع اللون ضوء ونور مقارن للون
فلا وهؤلاء إنما نبهوا على قيام النور بالمتلونات بالتفرقة التي يدركونها
بين الظل وموضع النور وبين الليل والنهار فإن الشمس لما تصور غيبتها بالليل
واحتجابها بالأجسام المظلمة بالنهار انقطع أثرها عن المتلونات فأدركت
التفرقة بين المتأثر المستضيء بها وبين المظلم المحجوب عنها فعرف وجود
النور بعدم النور إذا أضيف حالة العدم إلى حالة الوجود فأدركت التفرقة مع
بقاء الألوان في الحالتين ولو أطبق نور الشمس كل الأجسام الظاهرة لشخص ولم
تغب الشمس حتى يدرك التفرقة لتعذر عليه معرفة كون النور
شيئا موجودا زائدا على الألوان مع أنه أظهر الأشياء بل هو الذي به يظهر
جميع الأشياء
ولو تصور لله تعالى وتقدس عدم أو غيبة عن بعض الأمور لانهدت السموات
والأرض وكل ما انقطع نوره عنه ولأدركت التفرقة بين الحالتين وعلم وجوده
قطعا ولكن لما كانت الأشياء كلها متفقة في الشهادة والأحوال كلها مطردة على
نسق واحد كان ذلك سببا لخفائه فسبحان من احتجب عن الخلق بنوره وخفي عليهم
بشدة ظهوره فهو الظاهر الذي لا أظهر منه وهو الباطن الذي لا أبطن منه تنبيه
لا تتعجبن من هذا في صفات الله تعالى وتقدس فإن المعنى الذي به الإنسان
إنسان ظاهر باطن فإنه ظاهر إن استدل عليه بأفعاله المرتبة المحكمة باطن إن
طلب من إدراك الحس فإن الحس إنما يتعلق بظاهر بشرته وليس الإنسان إنسانا
بالبشرة المرئية منه بل لو تبدلت تلك البشرة بل سائر أجزائه فهو هو
والأجزاء متبدلة ولعل أجزاء كل إنسان بعد كبره غير الأجزاء التي كانت فيه
عند صغره فإنها تحللت بطول الزمان وتبدلت بأمثالها بطريق الاغتذاء وهويته
لم تتبدل فتلك الهوية باطنة عن الحواس ظاهرة للعقل بطريق الاستدلال عليها
بآثارها وأفعالها

### | البر

هو المحسن والبر المطلق هو الذي منه كل مبرة وإحسان والعبد إنما يكون برا
بقدر ما يتعاطاه من البر ولا سيما بوالديه وأستاذه وشيوخه
روي  أن موسى عليه السلام لما كلمه ربه رأى رجلا قائما عند ساق
العرش فتعجب من علو مكانه فقال يا رب بم بلغ هذا العبد هذا المحل فقال
إنه كان لا يحسد عبدا من عبادي على ما آتيته وكان بارا بوالديه هذا بر
العبد فأما تفصيل بر الله تعالى وإحسانه إلى خلقه فيطول شرحه وفي بعض ما
ذكرناه ما ينبه عليه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓahara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Emergence, elevation, becoming manifest to sense or intellect; the opposite of concealment (khaftāʾ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In divine attribution, al-Ẓāhir denotes that whose existence and governance are evidenced by every sign (āyah), yet whose essence is not encompassed by perception.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for sensory visibility; metaphorical (majāz) for intellectual self-evidence through inference (istidlāl).
- Root: ب-ط-ن (baṭana)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Interiority, hiddenness, that which is not reached by outward sense.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): al-Bāṭin is He who is veiled from sensory apprehension yet disclosed to rational reflection through His effects.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the concealed; metaphorical for that which transcends the reach of the five senses.
- Root: ب-ر-ر (barra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Abundant goodness, beneficence, dutifulness, especially to parents.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): al-Barr is the One whose beneficence (iḥsān) encompasses all existents without exception, being absolute and unconditioned.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the doer of good; metaphorical for the One whose very essence is pure goodness, not merely an act.
- Sībawayh Rule: Relational Predication (al-ḍāfah al-maʿnawiyyah) — terms like ẓāhir and bāṭin are relative (muḍāf), requiring a second term (perceiver) to complete their sense; hence they admit of simultaneous but distinct applications.
chapters.translation:
### | The Outward (al-Ẓāhir) and the Inward (al-Bāṭin)

These two descriptions are likewise among the relative attributes, for the outward is outward with respect to something and inward with respect to something else; it is not both outward and inward from a single aspect. Rather, it is outward from one aspect in relation to a certain mode of perception, and inward from another aspect. For outwardness and inwardness are only relative to modes of perception. God, glorified and exalted, is inward if sought through the perception of the senses and the storehouse of imagination, and outward if sought through the storehouse of the intellect by way of inference (istidlāl).

If you say: "As for His being inward relative to sensory perception, that is evident; but as for His being outward to the intellect, that is obscure — for the outward is that concerning which there is no doubt and about whose perception people do not differ, whereas this matter has been the subject of much skepticism among creatures — so how can He be outward?" — Know that He is only hidden despite His manifestation because of the intensity of His manifestation. His manifestation is the cause of His hiddenness, and His light is the veil of His light. Everything that exceeds its limit is inverted into its opposite.

Perhaps you marvel at this statement and deem it remote, and you will not understand it except through an example. So I say: If you looked at a single word written by a scribe, you would infer from it that the scribe is knowing, powerful, hearing, and seeing, and you would derive from it certainty of the existence of these attributes. Nay, if you saw a single written word, there would befall you decisive certainty of the existence of a writer for it who is knowing, powerful, hearing, seeing, and living — and nothing indicated him except the form of a single word. And just as this word bears decisive testimony to the attributes of the writer, so there is no atom in the heavens and the earth — whether sphere, star, sun, moon, animal, plant, attribute, or thing qualified — except that it testifies of itself to its need for a Disposer (mudabbir) who disposed it, determined it, and specified it with the particularity of its attributes. Nay, a man does not look at any organ of his own body, any part of his parts, outward or inward — nay, at any attribute of his attributes or any state of his states that runs over him by compulsion without his choice — except that he sees it speaking in testimony to its Creator, its Subduer, and its Disposer. Likewise, everything he perceives by all his senses, whether in his essence or external to his essence.

Now, if things differed in their testimony — some testifying and some not — then certainty would be attained for all. But when the testimonies multiplied until they agreed, they became hidden and obscure due to the intensity of manifestation. Its example: the most manifest of things is what is perceived by the senses; the most manifest of what is perceived by the senses is what is perceived by the sense of sight; and the most manifest of what is perceived by the sense of sight is the light of the sun shining upon bodies, by which everything appears. So how should that by which everything appears not be itself apparent?

Yet this has been problematic for many creatures, so much so that they said: "Colored things contain nothing but their colors alone — blackness and redness. As for there being in them, along with the color, a light and radiance concomitant with the color — no." These people were only alerted to the existence of light in colored things by the distinction they perceive between shadow and the place of light, and between night and day. For when the sun sets — its absence being imagined by night and its concealment by opaque bodies by day — its effect upon colored things is cut off, and they perceive the distinction between what is affected and illuminated by it and what is darkened and veiled from it. Thus they come to know the existence of light by the absence of light, when the state of non-existence is compared to the state of existence; so they perceive the distinction while the colors remain in both states. But if the sun's light had covered all apparent bodies perpetually, and the sun never set so that the distinction could be perceived, it would be impossible for them to know that light is something existent, additional to colors — even though it is the most manifest of things; nay, it is that by which all things appear.

And if it were conceivable for God, exalted and sanctified, to have a non-existence or an absence from some matters, then the heavens and the earth would collapse, and everything from which His light was cut off would perish; and the distinction between the two states would be perceived, and His existence would be known with certainty. But since all things agree in testimony, and all states run uniformly upon a single pattern, that becomes the cause of His hiddenness. So glorified is He who is veiled from creatures by His light, and hidden from them by the intensity of His manifestation. He is the Outward than whom nothing is more outward, and the Inward than whom nothing is more inward.

**A Reminder (tanbīh):** Do not marvel at this regarding the attributes of God, exalted and sanctified. For the meaning by which a human is human is both outward and inward: it is outward if inferred from his ordered, well-wrought acts, and inward if sought through sensory perception. For sense only attaches to the surface of his skin, and a human is not human by the visible skin. Nay, even if that skin were replaced — nay, all his parts — he is still he, while the parts are replaced. Perhaps the parts of every human after his maturity are not the parts that were in him at his youth, for they dissolve over the long passage of time and are replaced by their likes through the way of nourishment — yet his identity (huwiyyah) has not changed. So that identity is inward to the senses, outward to the intellect by way of inference upon it through its traces and acts.

### | The Righteous (al-Barr)

He is the Beneficent (al-Muḥsin). The absolute Righteous (al-Barr al-muṭlaq) is He from whom comes every act of righteousness (birr) and beneficence (iḥsān). The servant is only righteous to the measure of the righteousness he practices — especially toward his parents, his teacher, and his elders.

It is related that when Moses, peace be upon him, spoke with his Lord, he saw a man standing at the leg of the Throne, and he marveled at the loftiness of his station. He said: "O Lord, by what did this servant attain this station?" He said: "He never envied any of My servants for what I gave him, and he was righteous (barran) to his parents." This is the righteousness of the servant. As for the detailed account of God's righteousness and beneficence toward His creatures, its exposition would be lengthy; and in what we have mentioned there is sufficient indication of it.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | التواب

هو الذي يرجع إلى تيسير أسباب التوبة لعباده مرة بعد أخرى بما يظهر لهم
من آياته ويسوق إليهم من تنبيهاته ويطلعهم عليه من تخويفاته وتحذيراته حتى
إذا اطلعوا بتعريفه على غوائل الذنوب استشعروا الخوف بتخويفه فرجعوا إلى
التوبة فرجع إليهم فصل الله تعالى بالقبول تنبيه
من قبل معاذير المجرمين من رعاياه وأصدقائه ومعارفه مرة بعد أخرى فقد
تخلق بهذا الخلق وأخذ منه نصيبا

### | المنتقم

هو الذي يقصم ظهور العتاة وينكل بالجناة ويشدد العقاب على الطغاة وذلك
بعد الإعذار والإنذار وبعد التمكين والإمهال وهو أشد للانتقام من المعاجلة
بالعقوبة فإنه إذا عوجل بالعقوبة لم يمعن في المعصية فلم يستوجب غاية
النكال في العقوبة تنبيه
المحمود من انتقام العبد أن ينتقم من أعداء الله تعالى وأعدى الأعداء
نفسه وحقه أن ينتقم منها مهما قارفت معصية أو أخلت بعبادة كما نقل عن أبي
يزيد رحمه الله أنه قال تكاسلت نفسي علي في بعض الليالي عن بعض الأوراد
فعاقبتها بأن منعتها الماء سنة فهكذا ينبغي أن يسلك سبيل الانتقام

### | العفو

هو الذي يمحو السيئات ويتجاوز عن المعاصي وهو قريب من الغفور ولكنه أبلغ
منه فإن الغفران ينبئ عن الستر والعفو ينبئ عن المحو والمحو أبلغ من الستر
تنبيه
وحظ العبد من ذلك لا يخفى وهو أن يعفو عن كل من ظلمه بل يحسن إليه كما
يرى الله تعالى محسنا في الدنيا إلى العصاة والكفرة غير معاجل لهم بالعقوبة
بل ربما يعفو عنهم بأن يتوب عليهم وإذا تاب عليهم محا سيئاتهم إذ التائب من
الذنب كمن لا ذنب له وهذا غاية المحو للجناية

### | الرؤوف

ذو الرأفة والرأفة شدة الرحمة فهو بمعنى الرحيم مع المبالغة فيه وقد سبق
الكلام عليه

### | مالك الملك

هو الذي ينفذ مشيئته في مملكته كيف شاء وكما شاء إيجادا وإعداما وإبقاء
وإفناء والملك هاهنا بمعنى المملكة والمالك بمعنى القادر التام
القدرة والموجودات كلها مملكة واحدة وهو مالكها وقادرها وإنما كانت
الموجودات كلها مملكة واحدة لأنها مرتبطة بعضها ببعض فإنها وإن كانت كثيرة
من وجه فلها وحدة من وجه ومثاله بدن الإنسان فإنه مملكة لحقيقة الإنسان وهي
أعضاء كثيرة مختلفة ولكنها كالمتعاونة على تحقيق غرض مدبر واحد فكانت مملكة
واحدة فكذلك العالم كله كشخص واحد وأجزاء العالم كأعضائه وهي متعاونة على
مقصود واحد وهو إتمام غاية الخير الممكن وجوده على ما اقتضاه الجود الإلهي
ولأجل انتظامها على ترتيب متسق وارتباطها برابطة واحدة كانت مملكة واحدة
والله تعالى مالكها فقط
ومملكة كل عبد بدنه خاصة فإذا نفذت مشيئته في صفات قلبه وجوارحه فهو مالك
مملكة نفسه بقدر ما أعطي من القدرة عليها

### | ذو الجلال والإكرام

هو الذي لا جلال ولا كمال إلا وهو له ولا كرامة ولا مكرمة إلا وهي صادرة
منه فالجلال له في ذاته والكرامة فائضة منه على خلقه وفنون إكرامه خلقه لا
تكاد تنحصر وتتناهى وعليه دل قوله تعالى ولقد كرمنا بني آدم 17 سورة
الإسراء الآية 70

### | الوالي

هو الذي دبر أمور الخلق ووليها أي تولاها وكان مليا بولايتها وكأن
الولاية تشعر بالتدبير والقدرة والفعل وما لم يجتمع جميع ذلك فيه لم ينطلق
اسم الوالي عليه ولا والي للأمور إلا الله سبحانه وتعالى فإنه المتفرد
بتدبيرها أولا والمنفذ للتدبير بالتحقيق ثانيا والقائم عليها بالإدامة
والإبقاء ثالثا

### | المتعالي

بمعنى العلي مع نوع من المبالغة وقد سبق معناه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, recurrence; repentance as a turning back to God
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine facilitation of the servant's return; God's recurrent gracious initiative
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for God's act of turning; metaphorical for His enabling causes
- Root: ن-ق-م (n-q-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Punishment, retribution; breaking and crushing in requital
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Retributive justice after warning; distinct from hasty vengeance
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for divine chastisement; metaphorical for the soul's self-discipline
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Erasure, obliteration; leaving off blame
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Erasure of sins surpassing mere covering (ghufrān)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for blotting out; metaphorical for complete remission
- Root: ر-أ-ف (r-ʾ-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intense mercy, tenderness
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Mercy intensified to its utmost degree
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for divine compassion; superlative of raḥīm
- Root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dominion, possession; sovereign power
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Complete capacity over all existents as one unified realm
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for God's sole sovereignty; metaphorical for the servant's rule over his body
- Root: ج-ل-ل (j-l-l) & ك-ر-م (k-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Majesty, grandeur; nobility, generosity
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Glory intrinsic to God; bounty flowing from Him to creation
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for divine attributes; metaphorical for their manifestation in creatures
- Root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Governance, undertaking, proximity
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Combined administration, power, and act in sole divine agency
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for God's exclusive governance; metaphorical for delegated oversight
- Root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Height, elevation, transcendence
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Supremacy beyond all comparison, with intensified force
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for divine exaltation; metaphorical for rank, not spatial height
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal sentence with predicate emphasis (al-mubtadaʾ wa al-khabar) — each divine name is introduced as a defined subject with a predicate clause clarifying its semantic scope; the pattern "هو الذي" (He is the One who) establishes a restrictive definition, requiring the predicate to specify the essential act or attribute without ellipsis.
chapters.translation:
### The Pardoning (al-Tawwāb)

He is the One who returns to facilitating the means of repentance for His servants, time after time, through what He manifests to them of His signs, what He conveys to them of His admonitions, and what He discloses to them of His warnings and cautions — until, when they have discerned, through His definition, the perils of sins, they come to feel fear through His terrifying, and so they turn in repentance, whereupon He turns to them with acceptance. A note of awareness: whoever pardons the excuses of criminals among his subjects, his friends, and his acquaintances, time after time, has indeed adorned himself with this trait and taken a share of it.

### The Avenger (al-Muntaqim)

He is the One who breaks the backs of the obstinate, inflicts exemplary punishment upon the offenders, and intensifies chastisement upon the tyrants — and this only after the excuse has been cut off and the warning delivered, and after empowerment and respite have been granted. For this is more severe in vengeance than hastening the punishment; since if one were hastened to punishment, he would not persist deeply in disobedience, and thus would not merit the utmost extremity of exemplary penalty. A note of awareness: the praiseworthy form of a servant's vengeance is that he take vengeance upon the enemies of God — and the most hostile of enemies is his own self. It is his right to take vengeance upon it whenever it commits a disobedience or neglects an act of worship — as is transmitted from Abū Yazīd (may God have mercy on him), who said: "My self grew sluggish with me one night regarding certain litanies, so I punished it by denying it water for a year." Thus should one tread the path of vengeance.

### The Pardoning (al-ʿAfuww)

He is the One who erases evil deeds and passes over transgressions. This is near to the Forgiving (al-Ghafūr), but more emphatic than it; for forgiveness (ghufrān) signifies covering, while pardon (ʿafw) signifies erasure — and erasure is more emphatic than covering. A note of awareness: the servant's share of this is not hidden — namely, that he pardon everyone who has wronged him, nay, even do good to him, just as he sees God — exalted — doing good in this world to the disobedient and the disbelievers, not hastening them to punishment; rather, He may even pardon them by granting them repentance, and when He grants them repentance, He erases their evil deeds — for the one who repents of a sin is like one who has no sin. And this is the utmost degree of erasing the offense.

### The Compassionate (al-Raʾūf)

Possessor of compassion (raʾfah), and compassion is the intensity of mercy. Thus it carries the meaning of the Merciful (al-Raḥīm) with intensification therein — and the discourse on this has already preceded.

### The Owner of Sovereignty (Mālik al-Mulk)

He is the One who executes His will in His dominion, however He wills and as He wills — in bringing into being and annihilating, in preserving and destroying. "Dominion" (mulk) here means the realm (mamlakah), and "Owner" (mālik) means the one of complete capacity (al-qādir al-tāmm al-qudrah). All existents constitute a single realm, and He is its Owner and its Powerful One. And the reason all existents constitute a single realm is that they are interconnected with one another; for though they are many in one respect, they possess unity in another respect. Its example is the human body: it is a realm for the reality of the human being, being many diverse organs, yet they are as if cooperating in realizing the purpose of a single director — thus it is one realm. Likewise, the entire world is like a single person, and the parts of the world are like his organs, cooperating toward a single aim — namely, the completion of the utmost good possible in existence, according to what divine generosity (al-jūd al-ilāhī) has necessitated. And because of their ordering upon a consistent arrangement and their linkage by a single bond, they constitute one realm — and God — exalted — is its sole Owner.

And the realm of every servant is his body in particular. So when his will is executed upon the traits of his heart and his bodily members, he is the owner of his own realm, to the extent of the capacity granted him over it.

### The Lord of Majesty and Bounty (Dhū al-Jalāl wa al-Ikrām)

He is the One who has no majesty or perfection but that it belongs to Him, and no honor or act of honoring but that it issues from Him. Thus majesty (jalāl) is His in His essence, and bounty (karāmah) flows from Him upon His creation. The varieties of His honoring of His creatures can scarcely be encompassed or terminated — and upon this the saying of God — exalted — indicates: {«وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِي آدَمَ»} "And indeed We have honored the children of Adam" (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ, 17:70).

### The Governor (al-Wālī)

He is the One who administered the affairs of creation and undertook them — that is, assumed charge of them — and was fully competent for their administration. It is as if governance (wilāyah) intimates administration (tadbīr), power (qudrah), and act (fiʿl); and unless all of these are combined in one, the name "Governor" is not applied to him. And there is no governor of affairs but God — glorified and exalted — for He alone is unique in administering them, firstly; the executor of administration in actuality, secondly; and the one who sustains them in continuance and preservation, thirdly.

### The Most Exalted (al-Mutaʿālī)

It carries the meaning of the High (al-ʿAlī) with a kind of intensification — and its meaning has already preceded.

chapters.title_en: Section 33: The Equitable (al-Muqsiṭ), The Unifier (al-Jāmiʿ), The Self-Sufficient & The Enricher (al-Ghanī al-Mughnī), The Withholder (al-Māniʿ)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | المقسط

هو الذي ينتصف للمظلوم من الظالم وكما له في أن يضيف إلى إرضاء المظلوم
إرضاء الظالم وذلك غاية العدل والإنصاف ولا يقدر عليه إلا الله سبحانه
وتعالى
ومثاله ما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه بينما هو جالس إذ ضحك  حتى
بدت ثناياه فقال عمر رضي الله عنه بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله ما الذي
أضحكك قال رجلان من أمتي جثيا بين يدي رب العزة فقال أحدهما يا رب خذ لي
مظلمتي من هذا فقال الله عز وجل رد على أخيك مظلمته فقال يا رب لم يبق لي
من حسناتي شيء فقال عز وجل للطالب كيف تصنع بأخيك لم يبق من حسناته شيء
فقال يا رب فليحمل عني من أوزاري ثم فاضت عينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم بالبكاء وقال إن ذلك ليوم عظيم يوم يحتاج الناس إلى أن يحمل عنهم من
أوزارهم قال فيقول الله عز وجل للمتظلم ارفع بصرك فانظر في الجنان فقال يا
رب أرى مدائن من فضة وقصورا من ذهب مكللة باللؤلؤ لأي نبي هذا أو لأي صديق
أو لأي شهيد قال الله عز وجل هذا لمن أعطى الثمن قال يا رب ومن يملك ذلك
قال أنت تملكه قال بماذا يا رب قال بعفوك عن أخيك قال يا رب قد عفوت عنه
قال الله عز وجل خذ بيد أخيك فأدخله الجنة ثم قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اتقوا
الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم فإن الله تبارك وتعالى يصلح بين المؤمنين يوم
القيامة
فهذا سبيل الانتصاف والإنصاف ولا يقدر على مثله إلا رب الأرباب وأوفر
العباد حظا من هذا الاسم من ينتصف أولا من نفسه ثم لغيره من غيره ولا ينتصف
لنفسه من غيره

### | الجامع

هو المؤلف بين المتماثلات والمتباينات والمتضادات
أما جمع الله المتماثلات فكجمعه الخلق الكثير من الإنس على ظهر الأرض
وكحشره إياهم في صعيد القيامة
وأما المتباينات فكجمعه بين السموات والكواكب والهواء والأرض والبحار
والحيوانات والنبات والمعادن المختلفة كل ذلك متباين الأشكال والألوان
والطعوم والأوصاف وقد جمعها في الأرض وجمع بين الكل في العالم وكذلك جمعه
بين العظم والعصب والعرق والعضلة والمخ والبشرة والدم وسائر الأخلاط في بدن
الحيوان
وأما المتضادات فكجمعه بين الحرارة والبرودة والرطوبة واليبوسة في أمزجة
الحيوانات وهي متنافرات متعاديات  وذلك أبلغ وجوه الجمع
وتفصيل جمعه لا يعرفه إلا من يعرف تفصيل مجموعاته في الدنيا والآخرة وكل
ذلك مما يطول شرحه تنبيه
الجامع من العباد من جمع بين الآداب الظاهرة في الجوارح وبين الحقائق
الباطنة في القلوب فمن كملت معرفته وحسنت سيرته فهو الجامع ولذلك قيل
الكامل من لا يطفئ نور معرفته نور ورعه وكان الجمع بين الصبر
والبصيرة متعذر لذلك ترى صبورا على الزهد والورع لا بصيرة له وترى ذا
بصيرة لا صبر له والجامع من جمع بين الصبر والبصيرة والسلام

### | الغني المغني

الغني هو الذي لا تعلق له بغيره لا في ذاته ولا في صفات ذاته بل يكون
منزها عن العلاقة مع الأغيار فمن تتعلق ذاته أو صفات ذاته بأمر خارج من
ذاته يتوقف عليه وجوده أو كماله فهو فقير محتاج إلى الكسب ولا يتصور ذلك
إلا لله سبحانه وتعالى
والله عز وجل هو المغني أيضا ولكن الذي أغناه لا يتصور أن يصير بإغنائه
غنيا مطلقا فإن أقل أموره أنه محتاج إلى المغني فلا يكون غنيا بل يستغني عن
غير الله بأن يمده بما يحتاج إليه لا بأن يقطع عنه أصل الحاجة والغني
الحقيقي هو الذي لا حاجة له إلى أحد أصلا والذي يحتاج ومعه ما يحتاج فهو
غني بالمجاز وهو غاية ما يدخل في الإمكان في حق غير الله سبحانه وتعالى
وأما فقد الحاجة فلا ولكن إذا لم يبق حاجة إلا إلى الله تعالى سمي غنيا
ولو لم يبق له أصل الحاجة لما صح قوله تعالى والله الغني وأنتم الفقراء 47
سورة محمد الآية 38 ولولا أنه يتصور أن يستغني عن كل شيء سوى الله عز وجل
لما صح لله تعالى وصف المغني

### | المانع

هو الذي يرد أسباب الهلاك والنقصان في الأديان والأبدان بما يخلقه من
الأسباب المعدة للحفظ وقد سبق معنى الحفيظ وكل حفظ فمن ضرورته
منع ودفع فمن فهم معنى الحفيظ فهم معنى المانع والمنع إضافة إلى السبب
المهلك والحفظ إضافة إلى المحروس عن الهلاك  وهو مقصود المنع وغايته إذ
المنع يراد للحفظ والحفظ لا يراد للمنع فكل حافظ مانع وليس كل مانع حافظا
إلا إذا كان مانعا مطلقا لجميع أسباب الهلاك والنقص حتى يحصل الحفظ من
ضرورته
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق س ط (q-s-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes evenness, fairness, and the act of dividing equitably; al-qisṭ is the just measure or portion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, al-Muqsiṭ is the One who restores the wronged party's right from the wrongdoer, establishing cosmic justice (ʿadl) as an attribute of divine action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "one who gives each his due share"; metaphorically extended to divine recompense on the Day of Judgment where no soul is wronged.
- Root: ج م ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bring together, assemble, unite, or reconcile disparate elements into a coherent whole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine unification (jamʿ) spans ontological categories—assembling like, unlike, and contrary things—manifesting God's absolute power over all composition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal gathering of physical objects; metaphorical for the soul's integration of outward conduct (ādāb ẓāhirah) with inward realities (ḥaqāʾiq bāṭinah).
- Root: غ ن ي (gh-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Freedom from need, sufficiency, independence; the opposite of poverty (faqr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): True wealth (ghinā) is absolute self-sufficiency in essence and attributes—a prerogative of God alone; creatures possess only relative, metaphorical wealth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal independence from all causes; metaphorical when a creature's needs are reduced to God alone, yet still contingent upon Him.
- Root: م ن ع (m-n-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To prevent, hinder, withhold, or repel something harmful.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine prevention (manʿ) is the repulsion of destructive causes through the creation of protective means—an aspect of preservation (ḥifẓ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal act of blocking; metaphorical in that prevention is subordinate to preservation, as the former is a means and the latter an end.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Complementarity (Takāmul) — The syntactic relationship between two terms where one (al-manʿ) is defined by its purpose (al-ḥifẓ), establishing a logical hierarchy: "every preserver is a preventer, but not every preventer is a preserver" unless prevention is absolute.
chapters.translation:
### | The Equitable (al-Muqsiṭ)

I say: He is the One who causes the wronged to obtain justice from the wrongdoer. And just as it is within His power to add the satisfaction of the wrongdoer to the satisfaction of the wronged—and that is the utmost limit of justice and equity—none is capable of this save God, Glorified and Exalted be He.

An example of this is what was related from the Prophet, peace be upon him: While he was sitting, he laughed until his molars became visible. ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God, what has made you laugh?" He said: "Two men of my community knelt before the Lord of Might. One of them said: 'O Lord, take my due from this one.' God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Return to your brother his due.' He said: 'O Lord, nothing of my good deeds remains.' God, Mighty and Majestic, said to the claimant: 'What will you do with your brother when nothing of his good deeds remains?' He said: 'O Lord, then let him carry from my burdens.'" Then the eyes of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, overflowed with tears, and he said: "That is indeed a tremendous day—a day when people will need others to carry from their burdens." He said: "Then God, Mighty and Majestic, says to the claimant: 'Raise your gaze and look upon the gardens.' He says: 'O Lord, I see cities of silver and palaces of gold adorned with pearls—for which prophet is this, or which veracious one, or which martyr?' God says: 'This is for the one who pays the price.' He says: 'O Lord, who possesses that?' He says: 'You possess it.' He says: 'By what, O Lord?' He says: 'By your pardoning of your brother.' He says: 'O Lord, I have pardoned him.' God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Take your brother's hand and admit him into Paradise.'" Then he, peace be upon him, said: "Fear God and set right the matter between yourselves, for God, Blessed and Exalted, will set right the matter between the believers on the Day of Resurrection."

This, then, is the path of obtaining justice and rendering equity, and none is capable of its like save the Lord of lords. The servant with the greatest share of this name is the one who first obtains justice from himself against himself, then for others against others—but does not seek justice for himself from others.

### | The Unifier (al-Jāmiʿ)

I say: He is the One who composes together the similar, the dissimilar, and the contrary.

As for God's uniting the similar—it is like His gathering the vast multitude of humankind upon the face of the earth, and like His mustering them upon the plain of the Resurrection.

As for the dissimilar—it is like His bringing together the heavens, the stars, the air, the earth, the seas, the animals, the plants, and the diverse minerals. All of these are disparate in forms, colors, tastes, and qualities, yet He has gathered them upon the earth and united the whole within the world. Likewise is His composition of bone, sinew, vein, muscle, marrow, skin, blood, and the remaining humors within the body of the animal.

As for the contrary—it is like His uniting heat and cold, moisture and dryness within the temperaments of animals, though these are mutually repugnant and hostile. And that is the most profound mode of unification.

The detailed account of His uniting is known only to one who knows the detailed account of what He has united in this world and the Hereafter—and all of that would be lengthy to explain.

**A Reminder:** The unifier among servants is the one who unites the outward etiquettes (ādāb ẓāhirah) in the limbs with the inward realities (ḥaqāʾiq bāṭinah) in the hearts. Whoever's knowledge is perfected and whose conduct is virtuous—he is the unifier. For this reason it was said: "The perfect one is he whose light of knowledge does not extinguish the light of his piety." And the union of patience (ṣabr) and insight (baṣīrah) is difficult—thus you see one patient in asceticism and piety who has no insight, and you see one possessed of insight who has no patience. The unifier is the one who unites patience and insight—and peace.

### | The Self-Sufficient & The Enricher (al-Ghanī al-Mughnī)

I say: The Self-Sufficient (al-Ghanī) is the One who has no attachment to another—neither in His essence nor in the attributes of His essence. Rather, He is exalted above all relation with others. Whoever's essence or the attributes of his essence are attached to something external to himself, upon which his existence or perfection depends—he is poor (faqīr), in need of acquisition. And that is conceivable only of God, Glorified and Exalted be He.

God, Mighty and Majestic, is also the Enricher (al-Mughnī). But the one whom He enriches cannot, by His enrichment, become absolutely self-sufficient. For the least of his circumstances is that he remains in need of the Enricher—thus he is not self-sufficient. Rather, he becomes independent of other than God in that He supplies him with what he needs—not in that the root of need is cut off from him. The truly self-sufficient is the one who has no need of anyone whatsoever. As for the one who has needs and possesses what he needs—he is self-sufficient metaphorically (bi-l-majāz). And that is the utmost possible extent for other than God, Glorified and Exalted be He.

As for the absence of need altogether—that is not possible. But when no need remains except toward God, Exalted, he is called self-sufficient. Were there no remaining root of need at all, then His saying, Exalted: {«And God is the Self-Sufficient, and you are the poor»} (Sūrat Muḥammad 47:38) would not be sound. And were it not conceivable that one become independent of everything save God, Mighty and Majestic, then the description of God, Exalted, as the Enricher would not be sound.

### | The Withholder (al-Māniʿ)

I say: He is the One who repels the causes of destruction and deficiency in religions and bodies through what He creates of means prepared for preservation. The meaning of the Preserver (al-Ḥafīẓ) has already preceded. And every preservation necessarily entails a withholding and a repelling. So whoever understands the meaning of the Preserver understands the meaning of the Withholder. Withholding is relative to the destructive cause, while preservation is relative to what is guarded from destruction—and that is the purpose of withholding and its end. For withholding is sought for the sake of preservation, while preservation is not sought for the sake of withholding. Thus every preserver is a withholder, but not every withholder is a preserver—unless he is an absolute withholder of all causes of destruction and deficiency, such that preservation results from it necessarily.
